Name: Common Sensor Rolling Shutter Terms
Description: The Common Sensor Rolling Shutter terms TRE (Section M.6.2) provides time as a function of pixel location across a frame. Time is then used by the model to interpolate ephemeris and attitude from the CSEPHB and CSATTB DESs, respectively. Time differences (i.e., delta-T or DT) with respect to the frame reference time are modeled by blocks such that each corner of the block is assigned a DT value.

N_RS_ROW_BLOCKS.Name: Blocks in Row Dimension
N_RS_ROW_BLOCKS.Description: This field contains the number of equally spaced blocks in the row dimension.

M_RS_COLUMN_BLOCKS.Name: Blocks in Column Dimension
M_RS_COLUMN_BLOCKS.Description: This field contains the number of equally spaced blocks in the column dimension.

RS_DT_1<M_RS_COLUMN_BLOCKS<N_RS_ROW_BLOC.Name: Rolling Shutter Delta Time
RS_DT_1<M_RS_COLUMN_BLOCKS<N_RS_ROW_BLOC.Description: This field provides the rolling shutter delta time with respect to the image reference time assiated witht he frame of interest for the four corners of block nm. RS_DT_1: Upper-left corner, RS_DT_2: Upper-right corner, RS_DT_3: Lower-right corner, RS_DT_4: Lower-left corner. The number of digits before and after the decimal point may change, i.e., the decimal point may float, as long as all 12 bytes are specified. For example, if the value is 15.4, then the formatted field value may be +15.40000000, +000000015.4, +00015.40000, or some other variant. However, the data provider should place the radix so that the number of digits after the decimal point represents the precision of the provided value. Therefore, if the precision of the measurement is to the second decimal place, then the appropriate value is +00000015.40.
